subject: Emit latency & streaming probe — summarizing TTFT targets and next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Redding <sam@edgepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Emit latency & streaming probe — summarizing TTFT targets and next steps

Hi Sam — thanks again for the demo and the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an agreed plan: 

1) Performance targets you gave:
   - Time-to-first-token (TTFT): <= 80ms p50, <= 180ms p95 for single-message generation at 1–2k tokens output.
   - Sustained throughput target: 250 requests/sec (peak bursts to 400 rps for <5m).
   - Concurrent sessions: ~1000 simultaneous WebSocket SSE streams.

2) Streaming & protocol preference:
   - You preferred Server-Sent Events (SSE) for browser-based checkout flows; WebSocket acceptable for backend-to-backend streaming.
   - Chunk cadence: you want early partial output every ~40–80ms where feasible (we'll qualify cadence vs cost).

3) Risks & things to validate on our side:
   - TTFT measured from your edge to first token emitted (includes connection handshake for WS/SSE).
   - KV cache priming for long-context prompts may change P95 behavior — we'll test common prompt shapes.

4) Next steps (proposed schedule):
   - Today (Wed): We share a short probe plan + sample payloads (attached).
   - Thu: Redwood runs a focused TTFT + stream-cadence probe (controlled load) and shares metrics.
   - Fri: Joint sync to review results; iterate on chunk pacing and connection warm-up.

Attachments: ttft-probe-parameters.xlsx (probe payloads + sequence lengths), streaming-test-plan.md (test harness details).

Ask: can you confirm the burst window and whether 250 rps is sustained for 1 hour or a shorter ramp? Also confirm if you want us to bias initial tests to browser SSE or backend WS.

Best,

Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

——

Cc: EdgePay Platform Team <platform@edgepay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emit latency & streaming probe — summarizing TTFT targets and next steps

Thanks Irene — that matches our notes. A couple clarifications: 

- Burst window: we expect peak bursts of ~400 rps for up to 10 minutes (flash sales), sustained 250 rps for up to 45 minutes during normal peak.
- For first round, prioritize browser SSE (checkout UX). Backend WS only if SSE shows unacceptable head-of-line latency on our side.
- Target payloads: the checkout prompt average is ~320 tokens input; expected output usually 80–250 tokens depending on the flow.

Please prioritize TTFT (p50/p95) measured from connection open to first byte. If you can, include a cold-connection scenario and a warm-connection scenario (keepalive).

Also: any constraints on connection concurrency per Redwood Dedicated node? We want to understand scaling considerations for 1k simultaneous sessions.

Sam
Senior Product Manager, EdgePay
sam@edgepay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 01:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emit latency & streaming probe — internal ops check

Irene / Ben — quick internal note before we run Thu's probe: 

- Concurrency per node: Dedicated GPU instance (g4-like pool) can support ~120 SSE sessions with our current runtime configuration when the model is quantized to int8 and KV cache usage is moderate. For 1k concurrent SSE sessions we should plan for ~9-10 nodes plus a buffer for headroom. 
- Warm vs cold TCP/HTTP: connection warm-up (keepalives + prewarmed kernels) reduces TTFT p95 by ~40–70ms in our internal runs. Include warm and cold probes in the plan.
- Chunk cadence: 50ms cadence is achievable at low tokenization overhead, but for outputs that require heavy decoding (sampling/topk) cadence can slip to 80–120ms; we should log tokenization CPU during tests.

Ben: please confirm the test harness will capture per-connection handshake time and show SSE frame-level timestamps. Add any kernel-selection notes to the streaming-test-plan.md if you haven't yet.

Marissa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Emit latency & streaming probe — results sync prep and ask

Sam — thanks for the quick clarifications. We're on schedule to run the probe Thu morning (Redwood time). A few housekeeping items and one ask ahead of the sync: 

Housekeeping:
- Probe artifacts attached (ttft-probe-parameters.xlsx) — contains 6 sample payloads with varied input sizes and 3 cadence profiles (aggressive 40–60ms, balanced 60–80ms, conservative 80–120ms).
- Streaming test harness will emit per-frame timestamps and handshake times; we will upload raw traces to the Drive link included above.

Ask:
- Please confirm a single public IP range we should target for rate limits during the test, and whether your infra team needs us to route via a test VPC. This helps mimic real egress latency and TLS handshakes.

Planned deliverables for Fri sync:
- TTFT p50/p95 table for cold vs warm connections across the six payloads.
- Per-cadence breakdown showing median frame intervals, tokenization CPU, and end-to-end client-visible first-byte latency.
- A recommendation section: node counts (for Dedicated) and an early fallback policy (model variant or quantization) if p95 > target.

If that's all good, I'll ask Ben to run the controlled load Thu 09:00-10:30 PT and share the dashboard links during the sync.

Best,
Irene
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
